priya: Bringing up lexicon-multi-small (multilingual embed) in staging. Saw strange language-specific regressions after INT4 asymmetric quant. Posting quick numbers and config.

priya: Holdout (en/es/zh, 1k each), recall@5: fp16 en:0.882 es:0.860 zh:0.803
int8 en:0.878 (-0.4) es:0.854 (-0.7) zh:0.796 (-0.9)
int4 per-channel en:0.845 (-3.7) es:0.822 (-4.4) zh:0.718 (-10.6) <-- huge drop for zh
int4 asymmetric+zero-point en:0.852 (-3.3) es:0.835 (-2.9) zh:0.745 (-7.1)

oscar: Wow zh is hit hard. Could be tokenization or embedding norm differences across scripts. Did you run per-language normalization?

priya: Eval command: ```bash
python eval/multi_recall.py --model lexicon-multi-small --weights /mnt/models/lex-multi/int4_asym.pt \
  --holdouts en: s3://redwood-evals/multi/en_1k.jsonl,es: s3://redwood-evals/multi/es_1k.jsonl,zh: s3://redwood-evals/multi/zh_1k.jsonl \
  --batch 512 --sim cosine --normalize true --lang-split true
```
Normalization = length-norm per-embedding. No whitening.

helen: Two hypotheses: (1) calibration anchors are English-heavy so asymmetric zpt learned badly for CJK; (2) subword token coverage makes zh queries shorter -> quant noise hurts short sequences.

oscar: Can you share anchor distribution? If anchors 90% en, zpt will bias. Also try per-lang zero-point or per-script scale.

priya: Anchors used were s3://redwood-evals/anchors/multi_5k.jsonl (approx 70% en, 20% es, 10% zh). I'll run per-lang calib (5k per lang) and a per-lang PCA whitening to 128 dims. Also will test length-normalize before quant (simulate online centering).

helen: Also try a tiny MLP post-process (single linear + layernorm) trained on anchors to correct systematic bias between fp16 and int4. Cheap at runtime (128->128) and might recover zh.

oscar: Add synthetic char-noise test for zh: replace 10-30% chars with similar-looking characters to stress robustness. If int4 amplifies this, we know it's fragility.

eval-bot: Jobs queued: run_langcalib=1812345679-a (per-lang calib), run_pca=1812345679-b (per-lang PCA128), run_mlp=1812345679-c (post-MLP correction), started 1812345800, ETA ~25m. Will post per-lang recall curves and PCA/UMAP diffs.

priya: If per-lang calib recovers >5% for zh we can ship int4 with language-aware calibration for Dedicated regions. If not, fallback to int8 for CJK routes. Will update when eval-bot posts results. :mag:
